introduction: This spec defines the scoped rendering ref inference system for the `afspec` library (Python and Go implementations), which infers missing `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs` on subtasks to activate scoped rendering, emits validation warnings when refs are absent, updates generation templates to mandate ref population, and fixes a pre-existing Go fallback bug.

glossary.RenderIndividual: Go method on `*Spec` that renders the full spec without scoping, used as the unscoped fallback
glossary.RenderIndividualScoped: Go method on `*Spec` that mirrors `render_individual_scoped`, filtering rendered output to refs referenced by the target task group
glossary.Requirements: Model/struct within `Spec` holding the list of `Requirement` objects with acceptance criteria and edge cases
glossary.Spec: Top-level model/struct representing a complete agent-fox specification package, containing requirements, test spec, tasks, and architecture
glossary.Subtask: An individual unit of work within a `TaskGroup`, carrying `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs` lists
glossary.TaskGroup: A group of related subtasks within a spec, identified by an integer `id` and a `kind`
glossary.TaskGroupKind: Enum/type string classifying a `TaskGroup`; values include `TESTS`, `STANDARD`, `CHECKPOINT`, and `WIRING_VERIFICATION`
glossary.TestSpec: Model/struct within `Spec` holding test cases, property tests, edge case tests, and smoke tests
glossary.TraceabilityEntry: Model/struct linking a `task_id` to a `requirement_id` and `test_spec_id`, stored in `spec.tasks.traceability`
glossary.ValidationEntry: Go struct used for both errors and warnings in `ValidationResult`, carrying `Category`, `Check`, `Message`, `EntityID`, and `Artifact` fields
glossary.ValidationResult: Return type of `validate()` / `Validate()` containing `.valid`, `.errors`, and `.warnings` collections
glossary.ValidationWarning: A structured warning produced by `validate()` / `Validate()` describing a non-fatal spec quality issue
glossary.WIRING_VERIFICATION: A `TaskGroupKind` value indicating a task group that verifies integration wiring; excluded from missing-refs validation warnings
glossary._REQ_ID_RE: Python module-level compiled regex constant matching requirement and acceptance-criterion ID patterns
glossary._TS_ID_RE: Python module-level compiled regex constant matching test spec ID patterns
glossary._check_missing_subtask_refs: Python helper function added to `afspec.validation` that detects subtasks with empty `requirement_refs` or `test_spec_refs` and emits warnings
glossary._infer_refs_from_subtask_text: Python helper function that infers refs by regex-scanning subtask `title` and `details` for known ID patterns
glossary._infer_refs_from_traceability: Python helper function that infers refs by scanning `spec.tasks.traceability` for entries matching the target group prefix
glossary.checkMissingSubtaskRefs: Go helper function added to `golang/validate.go` that mirrors `_check_missing_subtask_refs`
glossary.generation_user_tasks.md: Agentspec prompt template file that instructs the agent how to generate task subtasks; modified to mandate ref population
glossary.partial inference: Condition where inference yields refs for only one ref type (requirement or test spec); scoped rendering still activates for the inferred type while the missing type falls back to full rendering
glossary.renderScopedTasks: Go method on `*Spec` that scopes the tasks section to a specific target group
glossary.render_individual: Python function in `afspec.render` that renders the full requirements and test spec without any scoping filter
glossary.render_individual_scoped: Python function in `afspec.render` that renders only the requirements and test spec sections referenced by a target task group's subtasks
glossary.reqIDRe: Go package-level compiled regex variable matching requirement ID patterns, defined via `regexp.MustCompile`
glossary.requirement_refs: List of requirement/acceptance-criterion IDs on a `Subtask` that controls which requirements are included in scoped rendering
glossary.scoped rendering: Rendering mode that filters requirements and test spec output to only those IDs referenced by the target task group's subtasks, reducing token usage
glossary.target_group: The integer ID of the `TaskGroup` passed to `render_individual_scoped` / `RenderIndividualScoped` to scope rendering
glossary.test_spec_refs: List of test spec IDs on a `Subtask` that controls which test cases are included in scoped rendering
glossary.text-based inference: Inference strategy that regex-scans subtask `title` and `details` fields for ID patterns matching known requirement and test spec IDs in the spec
glossary.traceability-based inference: Inference strategy that reads `spec.tasks.traceability` entries whose `task_id` starts with the target group prefix to collect `requirement_id` and `test_spec_id` values
glossary.tsIDRe: Go package-level compiled regex variable matching test spec ID patterns, defined via `regexp.MustCompile`
glossary.unscoped fallback: Rendering mode that dumps the entire requirements and test spec when no refs can be found or inferred, consuming ~15,000–20,000 extra tokens
glossary.validate: Python function in `afspec.validation` that validates a `Spec` and returns a `ValidationResult`
glossary.spec.tasks.traceability: The traceability array on the Tasks model linking requirement IDs to test spec IDs and task IDs
glossary.requirement_id: Field on TraceabilityEntry identifying the linked requirement
glossary.test_spec_id: Field on TraceabilityEntry identifying the linked test spec entry
glossary.task_id: Field on TraceabilityEntry identifying the linked task (format: group_id.subtask_number)
glossary.title: The title field on a Subtask model
glossary.details: The details field (list of strings) on a Subtask model
glossary.logging.getLogger(__name__): Python standard library call to obtain a module-level logger
glossary.var: Go keyword for declaring package-level variables
glossary.regexp.MustCompile: Go standard library function that compiles a regex pattern at package init time, panicking on invalid patterns
glossary.re.compile(...): Python standard library function that compiles a regex pattern into a reusable pattern object
glossary.kind == WIRING_VERIFICATION: Condition checking whether a TaskGroup's kind field equals the wiring_verification enum value
glossary.' and '.join(missing): Python idiom joining a list of field names with the string ' and '
glossary.{field_names}: Placeholder in the warning message template for the joined missing field names
glossary.nil: Go zero value for slices and pointers, equivalent to Python None for these types
glossary.None: Python singleton representing absence of a value
glossary.len(subtask.RequirementRefs) == 0: Go idiom checking whether a slice is empty (catches both nil and zero-length)
glossary.not subtask.requirement_refs: Python idiom checking whether a list is falsy (empty or None)
glossary.### Smoke test authoring: Existing section heading in generation_user_tasks.md that follows the insertion point
glossary.### Subtask refs (MANDATORY): New section heading to be added to generation_user_tasks.md
glossary.return s.RenderIndividual(): Current Go fallback that returns fully unscoped rendering (the bug being fixed)
glossary.s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup): Go method that renders tasks with only the target group expanded in full detail
glossary.RenderIndividual(): Go method on Spec that renders all artifacts without any scoping or filtering
glossary.traceability: The traceability array in tasks.json linking requirements to test specs and tasks
glossary.len(subtask.TestSpecRefs) == 0: Go idiom checking whether the test spec refs slice is empty
glossary.not subtask.test_spec_refs: Python idiom checking whether the test spec refs list is falsy
glossary.group.kind == TaskGroupKind.WIRING_VERIF: Python condition checking whether a group is a wiring verification group
glossary.group.Kind == TaskGroupKindWiringVerific: Go condition checking whether a group is a wiring verification group

requirements.title: Traceability-based ref inference in scoped rendering

user_story.goal: have scoped rendering automatically infer requirement and test spec refs from traceability data when subtask refs are empty
user_story.benefit: avoid the ~15,000-token unscoped fallback even for older specs that lack explicit refs

acceptance_criteria.action: invoke `_infer_refs_from_traceability` / `inferRefsFromTraceability` to filter `spec.tasks.traceability` entries whose `task_id` starts with `"{target_group}."` and collect their `requirement_id` and `test_spec_id` values as inferred refs
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` filtered to the inferred refs when at least one ref is found
acceptance_criteria.trigger: called with a `target_group` whose subtasks all have empty `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs`

acceptance_criteria.action: return only `requirement_id` and `test_spec_id` values from `TraceabilityEntry` records whose `task_id` starts with the string `"{target_group}."`, collecting them into separate sets/slices for requirement refs and test spec refs
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns two collections (inferred requirement refs, inferred test spec refs); both may be empty if no matching traceability entries exist

acceptance_criteria.action: activate scoped rendering using the inferred refs without proceeding to text-based inference or the `unscoped fallback`; in Python, emit a log message at INFO level via `logging.getLogger(__name__)`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string`; Python additionally emits an INFO log message
acceptance_criteria.state: traceability-based inference yields at least one requirement ref or test spec ref

edge_cases.action: return empty collections for both ref types, allowing the inference chain to proceed to text-based inference
edge_cases.return_contract: returns two empty collections (empty list/slice for requirement refs, empty list/slice for test spec refs)
edge_cases.error_condition: `spec.tasks.traceability` is empty or contains no entries whose `task_id` starts with `"{target_group}."`

edge_cases.action: skip the empty field value and only collect non-empty IDs into the respective ref collection
edge_cases.return_contract: returns collections containing only non-empty ID strings
edge_cases.error_condition: a `TraceabilityEntry` matching the target group prefix has an empty `requirement_id` or empty `test_spec_id` field

edge_cases.action: skip inference entirely and proceed with the existing scoped rendering logic using the explicit refs
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` using the explicit refs, identical to pre-inference behavior
edge_cases.error_condition: subtasks already have non-empty `requirement_refs` or `test_spec_refs` (explicit refs present)

requirements.title: Text-based ref inference in scoped rendering

user_story.goal: have scoped rendering infer refs by scanning subtask text when traceability data is also absent
user_story.benefit: maximize the chance of activating scoped rendering for specs that lack both explicit refs and traceability entries

acceptance_criteria.action: invoke `_infer_refs_from_subtask_text` / `inferRefsFromSubtaskText` to regex-scan the `title` and `details` fields of all subtasks in the target group using `_REQ_ID_RE` / `reqIDRe` and `_TS_ID_RE` / `tsIDRe`, then validate each match against the set of IDs actually present in the spec
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` filtered to validated matches when at least one validated match is found
acceptance_criteria.trigger: traceability-based inference returns empty collections for both ref types

acceptance_criteria.action: be defined as module-level compiled constants (Python: `re.compile(...)` assigned to `_REQ_ID_RE` and `_TS_ID_RE`; Go: package-level `var` block using `regexp.MustCompile` for `reqIDRe` and `tsIDRe`) so that regex compilation occurs once at import/init time and not per call

scan each subtask's `title` and all strings in `details` with `_REQ_ID_RE` / `reqIDRe` and `_TS_ID_RE` / `tsIDRe`, collect all regex matches, then filter to only those IDs that exist in the actual spec's known requirement IDs and test spec IDs respectively
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns two collections of validated ID strings (inferred requirement refs, inferred test spec refs); both may be empty

acceptance_criteria.action: activate scoped rendering using the text-inferred refs; in Python, emit a log message at INFO level via `logging.getLogger(__name__)`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string`; Python additionally emits an INFO log message
acceptance_criteria.state: text-based inference yields at least one validated requirement ref or test spec ref

edge_cases.action: discard all unvalidated matches and return empty collections, allowing the inference chain to fall through to the `unscoped fallback`
edge_cases.error_condition: regex matches are found in subtask text but none of the matched IDs exist in the spec's known requirement or test spec ID sets

edge_cases.action: return empty collections for both ref types
edge_cases.error_condition: subtask `title` and all `details` strings contain no text matching `_REQ_ID_RE` / `reqIDRe` or `_TS_ID_RE` / `tsIDRe`

edge_cases.action: scan only the `title` field; treat the absence of `details` as contributing zero matches
edge_cases.return_contract: returns collections based solely on `title` matches, validated against known spec IDs

requirements.title: Partial inference OR logic and unscoped fallback

user_story.goal: have scoped rendering activate even when only one ref type can be inferred, and fall back gracefully with scoped tasks when neither can be inferred
user_story.benefit: maximize token savings without discarding partially inferrable context, and ensure the Go fallback matches Python behavior

acceptance_criteria.action: activate scoped rendering using the inferred refs for the available type; render the missing ref type as a full section (equivalent to unscoped for that section only); do NOT fall through to the full `unscoped fallback`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` with the available ref type scoped and the missing ref type fully rendered
acceptance_criteria.state: inference yields refs for only one ref type (requirement refs but not test spec refs, or vice versa)

acceptance_criteria.action: fall back to full unscoped rendering but still scope the tasks section via `renderScopedTasks` / `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)` so that task output is always scoped to the target group
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` with full unscoped requirements and test spec but tasks scoped to the target group
acceptance_criteria.state: both traceability-based and text-based inference return empty collections for both ref types

acceptance_criteria.action: replace the previous `return s.RenderIndividual()` call with logic that calls `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)` to scope tasks, matching Python's existing fallback behavior
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a `map[string]string` with full unscoped requirements and test spec but tasks scoped to the target group, not a fully unscoped render
acceptance_criteria.trigger: the else-branch (no refs found and inference fails) is reached

edge_cases.action: proceed through the inference chain normally; if inference also yields no refs, fall back to the full unscoped render with scoped tasks (which will produce an empty tasks section for the missing group)
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` without panicking or raising an exception
edge_cases.error_condition: the `target_group` integer does not match any `TaskGroup` id in the spec

edge_cases.action: traceability inference returns empty collections; text inference proceeds against subtask text if subtasks exist; if no subtasks exist either, fall back to full unscoped render with scoped tasks
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` without panicking or raising an exception
edge_cases.error_condition: the spec has no `Tasks` / `traceability` data at all (nil/empty Tasks struct)

user_story.goal: receive a warning when subtasks have empty `requirement_refs` or `test_spec_refs`
user_story.benefit: surface the gap at generation time so specs can be fixed before they cause token waste during coding sessions

acceptance_criteria.action: invoke `_check_missing_subtask_refs` / `checkMissingSubtaskRefs` and append its results to the `ValidationResult` warnings collection
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a `ValidationResult` whose `.warnings` list includes one `ValidationWarning` / `ValidationEntry` per affected subtask
acceptance_criteria.trigger: called on a `Spec` containing subtasks with empty `requirement_refs` or `test_spec_refs`

acceptance_criteria.action: emit exactly one warning per subtask with message format: `"Subtask {id} has empty {field_names} — scoped rendering will fall back to full spec dump"` where `{field_names}` is `"requirement_refs"`, `"test_spec_refs"`, or `"requirement_refs and test_spec_refs"` depending on which fields are empty
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a list / slice of `ValidationWarning` / `ValidationEntry` objects, one per affected subtask
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a subtask has empty `requirement_refs` (Python: `not subtask.requirement_refs`; Go: `len(subtask.RequirementRefs) == 0`) or empty `test_spec_refs` (Python: `not subtask.test_spec_refs`; Go: `len(subtask.TestSpecRefs) == 0`)

acceptance_criteria.action: skip the entire `TaskGroup` without inspecting any of its subtasks
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns no warnings for any subtask belonging to a `WIRING_VERIFICATION` group
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a `TaskGroup` has `kind == WIRING_VERIFICATION` (Python: `group.kind == TaskGroupKind.WIRING_VERIFICATION`; Go: `group.Kind == TaskGroupKindWiringVerification`)

acceptance_criteria.action: use `' and '.join(missing)` (Python) or equivalent string join (Go) to produce the `{field_names}` portion of the warning message, ensuring consistent serialisation across both implementations

edge_cases.action: treat `None` / `nil` as empty using the defined emptiness check (`not subtask.requirement_refs` / `len(subtask.RequirementRefs) == 0`) and emit the matching warning
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a warning for the subtask as if the field were an empty list
edge_cases.error_condition: a subtask has `requirement_refs` set to `None` (Python) or `nil` (Go) rather than an explicit empty list

edge_cases.action: do NOT emit a warning for that subtask; placeholder-string cleanup is out of scope for this feature
edge_cases.return_contract: returns no warning for subtasks whose ref lists are non-empty, regardless of the content of the strings
edge_cases.error_condition: a subtask has non-empty `requirement_refs` containing placeholder strings such as `"TBD"` but not truly empty

edge_cases.action: return a `ValidationResult` with an empty warnings list from `_check_missing_subtask_refs` / `checkMissingSubtaskRefs`; no error is raised
edge_cases.return_contract: returns a `ValidationResult` with `.warnings` empty or containing only warnings from other checks
edge_cases.error_condition: the spec contains no `TaskGroup`s or all `TaskGroup`s are of kind `WIRING_VERIFICATION`

edge_cases.action: skip the entire group without emitting any warnings, even though the subtasks would otherwise qualify
edge_cases.return_contract: returns no warnings for any subtask in a `WIRING_VERIFICATION` group
edge_cases.error_condition: a `TaskGroup` of kind `WIRING_VERIFICATION` contains subtasks with empty refs

user_story.role: agent generating task subtasks from a prompt template
user_story.goal: be explicitly instructed that every subtask must have non-empty `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs`
user_story.benefit: prevent the token-waste problem at the source by ensuring newly generated specs always have populated refs

acceptance_criteria.action: contain a `### Subtask refs (MANDATORY)` section inserted after line 52 (the line reading "Reference both requirement IDs and test IDs from the previously generated artifacts in subtask `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs` fields.") and before the `### Smoke test authoring` section, with a blank line before and after the new section

include the exact body text: "Every subtask MUST have non-empty `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs`. These fields control scoped rendering — when they are empty, the entire requirements and test spec are dumped into the coding session (~15,000+ extra tokens). Populate both fields for every subtask by cross-referencing the requirement IDs and test spec IDs from the previously generated artifacts."

edge_cases.action: the insertion must be performed manually or the template update blocked until the anchor is confirmed; automated insertion must not silently insert at the wrong location
edge_cases.return_contract: The generation template file remains unchanged; no insertion is performed when the anchor text is absent
edge_cases.error_condition: the file does not contain line 52 with the expected anchor text (e.g., the file has been restructured)

requirements.title: Cross-implementation parity between Python and Go

user_story.goal: have the Python and Go implementations produce equivalent scoped rendering output and validation warnings for the same spec input
user_story.benefit: prevent divergence between implementations that would cause inconsistent behavior depending on which runtime is used

acceptance_criteria.action: follow the same inference chain order: (1) check explicit refs, (2) traceability-based inference, (3) text-based inference, (4) `unscoped fallback` with scoped tasks; both implementations must scope tasks in the fallback path

produce warning messages with identical format strings and field-name serialisation (`' and '.join(missing)` convention) so that test assertions can be written identically across both language test suites
omit the inference INFO log that Python emits (Go has no logging infrastructure); all other inference behavior must be identical to Python

edge_cases.action: this is the pre-existing bug being fixed; the fix replaces `return s.RenderIndividual()` with logic that calls `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)` in the fallback branch
edge_cases.return_contract: Go fallback returns `map[string]string` with scoped tasks, not a fully unscoped render
edge_cases.error_condition: the Go implementation diverges from Python by calling `RenderIndividual()` in the fallback branch instead of scoping tasks

correctness_properties.title: Inference never produces refs absent from the spec
correctness_properties.invariant: every ID in the inferred requirement refs and test spec refs returned by `_infer_refs_from_traceability` / `inferRefsFromTraceability` or `_infer_refs_from_subtask_text` / `inferRefsFromSubtaskText` exists in the spec's known requirement ID set or test spec ID set respectively

correctness_properties.title: Scoped rendering output is a subset of unscoped output
correctness_properties.for_any: spec and target group where inference or explicit refs yield non-empty collections
correctness_properties.invariant: the keys and content returned by `render_individual_scoped` / `RenderIndividualScoped` when scoped rendering activates are a subset of what `render_individual` / `RenderIndividual` would return for the same spec

correctness_properties.title: Fallback always scopes tasks
correctness_properties.for_any: spec and target group where both inference strategies return empty collections
correctness_properties.invariant: the tasks section in the fallback output is always scoped to the target group via `renderScopedTasks` / `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)` and never contains tasks from other groups

correctness_properties.title: Exactly one warning per affected subtask
correctness_properties.invariant: `_check_missing_subtask_refs` / `checkMissingSubtaskRefs` emits exactly one `ValidationWarning` / `ValidationEntry` per subtask with empty refs, never zero and never more than one per subtask, and emits zero warnings for subtasks in `WIRING_VERIFICATION` groups

correctness_properties.title: Warning message format is deterministic
correctness_properties.for_any: subtask with any combination of empty `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs`
correctness_properties.invariant: the warning message produced by `_check_missing_subtask_refs` / `checkMissingSubtaskRefs` always matches the template `"Subtask {id} has empty {field_names} — scoped rendering will fall back to full spec dump"` where `{field_names}` is one of `"requirement_refs"`, `"test_spec_refs"`, or `"requirement_refs and test_spec_refs"`

correctness_properties.title: Inference chain order is always traceability-first
correctness_properties.for_any: spec and target group with empty explicit refs
correctness_properties.invariant: text-based inference is never attempted when traceability-based inference returns non-empty collections for at least one ref type; the chain always evaluates traceability before text

correctness_properties.title: Regex patterns are compiled once at module/package init
correctness_properties.for_any: any number of calls to `render_individual_scoped` / `RenderIndividualScoped` in a single process
correctness_properties.invariant: `_REQ_ID_RE` and `_TS_ID_RE` (Python) and `reqIDRe` and `tsIDRe` (Go) are compiled exactly once at module import / package initialization time, not per function call

steps.action: calls `render_individual_scoped(spec, target_group=3)` / `spec.RenderIndividualScoped(3)` on a spec whose subtasks have empty `requirement_refs` and `test_spec_refs`
detects empty explicit refs on all subtasks in group 3 and invokes `_infer_refs_from_traceability` / `inferRefsFromTraceability` with target group prefix `"3."`
scans `spec.tasks.traceability` and returns non-empty requirement ref and test spec ref collections from matching `TraceabilityEntry` records
activates scoped rendering using the inferred refs; Python emits an INFO log via `logging.getLogger(__name__)`
receives a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` filtered to the inferred refs, consuming far fewer tokens than the `unscoped fallback`

execution_paths.title: Text-based inference activates scoped rendering when traceability is absent

steps.action: calls `render_individual_scoped(spec, target_group=2)` / `spec.RenderIndividualScoped(2)` on a spec with empty refs and no matching traceability entries
invokes `_infer_refs_from_traceability` / `inferRefsFromTraceability`; receives empty collections; proceeds to text-based inference
scans subtask `title` and `details` fields using `_REQ_ID_RE` / `reqIDRe` and `_TS_ID_RE` / `tsIDRe`, validates matches against known spec IDs, and returns non-empty validated ref collections
activates scoped rendering using the text-inferred refs; Python emits an INFO log
receives a scoped `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` filtered to validated text-inferred refs

execution_paths.title: Both inference strategies fail — scoped-tasks fallback

steps.action: calls `render_individual_scoped(spec, target_group=1)` / `spec.RenderIndividualScoped(1)` on a spec with empty refs, no traceability entries, and no ID patterns in subtask text
invokes `_infer_refs_from_traceability` / `inferRefsFromTraceability`; receives empty collections
invokes `_infer_refs_from_subtask_text` / `inferRefsFromSubtaskText`; receives empty collections after validation filtering
falls back to full unscoped requirements and test spec rendering but calls `renderScopedTasks` / `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)` to scope the tasks section to group 1
receives a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` with full requirements and test spec but tasks scoped to group 1

execution_paths.title: Validation warns on subtasks with empty refs

steps.action: calls `validate(spec)` / `spec.Validate()` on a spec containing subtasks with empty `requirement_refs` and/or `test_spec_refs`
invokes `_check_missing_subtask_refs` / `checkMissingSubtaskRefs` as part of the validation pipeline

iterates over all `TaskGroup`s, skips any with `kind == WIRING_VERIFICATION`, and for each remaining subtask with empty refs emits one `ValidationWarning` / `ValidationEntry` with the formatted message
appends the warnings to the `ValidationResult` and returns it to the caller

receives a `ValidationResult` whose `.warnings` list contains one entry per affected subtask, each with the message `"Subtask {id} has empty {field_names} — scoped rendering will fall back to full spec dump"`

execution_paths.title: Partial inference — only requirement refs inferred

steps.action: calls `render_individual_scoped(spec, target_group=4)` / `spec.RenderIndividualScoped(4)` on a spec where traceability entries exist for group 4 but only carry `requirement_id` values (no `test_spec_id`)
returns non-empty requirement refs and empty test spec refs

evaluates the OR condition (`inferred_req or inferred_ts`): requirement refs are non-empty, so scoped rendering activates; the requirements section is scoped to inferred refs; the test spec section is rendered in full
receives a `dict[str, str]` / `map[string]string` with requirements scoped to inferred refs and test spec fully rendered

error_handling.condition: Both `_infer_refs_from_traceability` and `_infer_refs_from_subtask_text` return empty collections for both ref types
error_handling.behavior: Fall back to full unscoped rendering for requirements and test spec, but scope the tasks section via `renderScopedTasks` / `s.renderScopedTasks(targetGroup)`; do not raise an exception or panic

error_handling.condition: A `TraceabilityEntry` has an empty `requirement_id` or `test_spec_id` string
error_handling.behavior: Skip the empty field value; only collect non-empty ID strings into the inferred ref collections

error_handling.condition: Text-based inference finds regex matches that do not correspond to any known ID in the spec
error_handling.behavior: Discard unvalidated matches; only retain IDs that exist in the spec's known requirement and test spec ID sets; if zero validated matches remain, fall through to the `unscoped fallback`

error_handling.condition: A subtask has `requirement_refs` or `test_spec_refs` set to `None` (Python) or `nil` (Go)
error_handling.behavior: Treat as empty using the defined emptiness check; emit a validation warning as if the field were an empty list

error_handling.condition: A subtask has non-empty refs containing only placeholder strings such as `"TBD"`
error_handling.behavior: Do not emit a validation warning and do not trigger inference; placeholder-string cleanup is out of scope
